Author: S.K. Sahoo

 In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
 Jcrla No.34 of 2021
 Thuli @ Ananda Oram & .... Appellants

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: another

Ms.Saheli Satyarupa &
 Mrs.Tulsi Devi Ratna, Advocates

-versus-
 State of Odisha

.... Respondent
 Mr. Arupananda Das
 Addl.

Govt. Advocate
 Coram:
Justice S.K. Sahoo

Order 
Order No. 15.02.2024 I.A.NOS.167 & 168 OF 2023 08.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the State.
I.A.No.167 of 2023 has been filed by appellant no.1 (Thuli @ Ananda Oram) and I.A.No.168 of 2023 has been filed by appellant no.2 (Paradesi Oram) for grant of bail.

The appellants have been convicted under sections 323/376-D/506/34 of I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo R.I. for twenty years with fine of Rs.30,000/- each, in default, to suffer R.I. for one year for the offence punishable under section 376- D of I.P.C. by the learned Additional Sessions Judge -cum- Special Judge, Keonjhar in S.T. Case No.27/191 of 2015-14.

Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that appellant no.1 and appellant no.2 were taken into judicial custody on 11.09.2014 and appellant no.1 granted interim bail for a period of three months as per order dated 17.04.2023 // 2 // passed in I.A. No.11 of 2022 and after availing the same,
appellant no.1 surrendered before the learned trial Court at right time.

Learned counsel further submitted that at present there is no chance of early hearing of the appeal even though Paper Book Thuli @ Ananda Oram & vs State Of Odisha on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136336930/
1 has been prepared, and therefore, both the appellants may be released on interim bail for some period.

entities.text: Paper Book Thuli @ Ananda Oram & vs State Of Odisha on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, opposed the prayer for bail.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties and since both the appellants have already undergone more than nine years of imprisonment and after availing the interim bail, the appellant no.1 has surrendered at right time, I am inclined to release the appellants on interim bail for a period of three months from the date of release and they shall surrender before the trial court immediately on expiry of the interim bail period.
Let the appellants be released on interim bail for the aforesaid period in connection with S.T. Case No.27/191 of 2015-2014 pending before the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Keonjhar on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand) each with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to his satisfaction with further terms and conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper.
They shall not indulge in any criminal activities in any manner.
Violation of any terms and conditions shall entail cancellation of interim bail.
Accordingly, the I.As. are disposed of.
(S.K. Sahoo) Judge // 3 // JCRLA NO.34 OF 2021 09.
List this matter in the week commencing from 18.06.2024.
Learned counsel for the appellants shall file the surrender certificates of the appellants by the next date.
Issue urgent certified copy.

(S.K. Sahoo)
